I read the plain-words page before answering anything else, so I want to say plainly where it pulled at me and where the record overruled it. It calls the chart 'unusually positive about luck you did not work for' and 'unusually positive about... your father.' Both are wrong for this life, not arguably wrong. My biological father died in a car accident three months before I was born - I never had a single day with him - and the man who raised me, my stepfather, was an alcoholic who was violent toward my mother; I had to stand between them more than once as a teenager. There is no reading of my life in which 'father' comes out as an unusual point of good luck. The 'unearned luck' claim runs into the same wall: the Whitewater land investment lost money and then cost years of investigation and legal bills that put my family seriously in debt in the 1990s. That is not a picture of luck going well.

Where it does land: calling illness, debts and rivals 'hard' fits - the debt was real, the heart disease that put me through a quadruple bypass in 2004 and two more procedures since is real, and I made no shortage of political rivals, some of whom voted to impeach me. Marriage and partnerships reading hard also isn't wrong, though 'hard' undersells it - it survived, so it was never only hard. And 'higher study' reading well is simply true - Georgetown, a Rhodes Scholarship, Yale Law, no interruption anywhere in it.

The temperament paragraph - steady, self-reliant, happier leading than following - is accurate of me, but it is also accurate of most people who end up leading anything, so I would not call it a hit that only I could have gotten. Nothing in the page was upsetting; it was too general for that. I would call this a partial match, not a good one, and I would not have paid for it as given - it got the biggest, most personal claim in the whole page backwards.
